root_cause.text: The mt76 remain-on-channel path introduced a self-deadlock by calling `mt76_set_channel()` from `mt76_remain_on_channel()` and `mt76_roc_complete()` while already holding `dev->mutex`, even though `mt76_set_channel()` also acquires the same mutex; additionally, `mac_work` could race and deadlock with the mutex, so it needed to be canceled before locking.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message explicitly says "`mt76_remain_on_channel()` and `mt76_roc_complete()` call `mt76_set_channel()` while already holding `dev->mutex`. Since `mt76_set_channel()` also acquires `dev->mutex`, this results in a deadlock`"; the diff fixes this by replacing `mt76_set_channel()` with `__mt76_set_channel()` in both sites and adding `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&phy->mac_work);` before `mutex_lock(&dev->mutex)` in `mt76_remain_on_channel()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use the internal channel restore helper when completing ROC to avoid the incorrect wrapper path.
intent_record.what: In mt76_roc_complete(), the call to mt76_set_channel(phy, &phy->main_chandef, false) was replaced with __mt76_set_channel(phy, &phy->main_chandef, false) under the same conditional check.
intent_record.how: At runtime, channel restoration after remain-on-channel completion now uses the internal channel-setting helper directly instead of the public wrapper, which changes the execution path while keeping the same conditional trigger and arguments.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending MAC work before remain-on-channel handling to avoid race conditions with concurrent PHY work.
intent_record.what: A call to `cancel_delayed_work_sync(&phy->mac_work);` was inserted in `mt76_remain_on_channel()` immediately after the `phy` null check and before acquiring `dev->mutex`.
intent_record.how: This forces any pending `phy->mac_work` delayed work to finish or be canceled before remain-on-channel processing continues, preventing that work from running concurrently and interfering with the channel change operation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Handle channel setup failures in remain-on-channel by cleaning up partial ROC state and aborting early.
intent_record.what: The code replaces a direct call to `mt76_set_channel(phy, &chandef, true);` with an assignment from `__mt76_set_channel(phy, &chandef, true)` into `ret`, and adds an error path that clears `mlink->mvif->roc_phy`, `phy->roc_vif`, and `phy->roc_link`, calls `mt76_put_vif_phy_link(phy, vif, mlink);`, and jumps to `out` when `ret` is nonzero.
intent_record.how: At runtime, channel setup for remain-on-channel now explicitly checks whether the channel change succeeded before proceeding. If setting the channel fails, the function unwinds the partially established ROC state and releases the vif/phy/link reference instead of continuing to signal readiness and schedule ROC work on a failed channel switch.

relevance_review.reason: The change addresses the ROC completion path, which is part of the reported deadlock root cause. Using the internal channel restore helper instead of the wrapper avoids calling the mutex-taking channel switch path while the mutex is already held, directly matching the vulnerability.

The group directly addresses part of the root cause by canceling pending mac_work before remain-on-channel handling, which prevents the mutex race/deadlock described. This matches the needed fix for the concurrent work deadlock aspect.

The group changes remain-on-channel handling and directly touch the same code path implicated in the deadlock. Although the stated intent is failure cleanup, it is still part of the ROC/channel setup flow where the mutex-related bug occurred, so it is related to the vulnerability root cause.

candidates.rationale: This remain-on-channel path calls mt76_set_channel() while already under dev->mutex, which can self-deadlock because mt76_set_channel() also acquires the same mutex.
The ROC completion path directly calls the wrapper mt76_set_channel() while the mutex is already held, creating the same self-deadlock condition described in the root cause.

This lock acquisition is the point where the remain-on-channel path enters the critical section before calling mt76_set_channel(), making the later recursive lock acquisition by mt76_set_channel() deadlock-prone.

vuln_statements.explanation: This ROC completion path calls mt76_set_channel() while dev->mutex is already held, causing a self-deadlock because mt76_set_channel() acquires the same mutex internally.

This is the critical lock acquisition that enters the remain-on-channel path's mutex-protected section before the later mt76_set_channel() call, enabling the recursive lock deadlock described in the root cause.
This remain-on-channel failure path invokes mt76_set_channel() while already under dev->mutex, which can self-deadlock for the same reason as the ROC completion path.

The code shown does not contain the fix of avoiding the nested lock or canceling `mac_work` before taking the mutex, so `is_fixed` is false.
